sections.label: Motion on justice system shortcomings
sections.summary: The Motion, triggered by Ms Parti Liyani's case, covers broader justice system issues and urges a two-pronged approach to shortcomings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Though this Motion was triggered by Ms Parti Liyani's case, our contributions will not be limited to issues from that case, but will include broader issues surrounding the justice system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to recognise that the current system, despite its strengths, does have shortcomings which need attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We call on the Government to take a two-pronged approach.

sections.label: Proposed Constitutional Commission
sections.summary: The speakers suggest setting up a Constitutional Commission led by a Supreme Court Judge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On these matters, we offer our perspective for consideration and suggest the setting up of a Constitutional Commission led by a Supreme Court Judge.

sections.label: Singapore Rule of Law ranking
sections.summary: Singapore ranks 12th out of 128 countries in the 2020 Rule of Law Index by the World Justice Project.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the 2020 Rule of Law Index compiled by the World Justice Project, Singapore ranks 12 out of 128 countries.

sections.label: Criminal justice government influence ranking
sections.summary: Singapore scores well on criminal investigation and corruption, but ranks 30th of 37 high-income countries on freedom from improper government influence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the factor of criminal justice, the Singapore system has done very well in sub-factors such as the effectiveness of criminal investigation and being free of corruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, on the critical sub-factor of whether the criminal system is free of improper government influence, the Singapore system is ranked poorly among high-income countries at 30th out of 37th and globally at 47th.

sections.label: Prison population education profile
sections.summary: MHA data showed nearly 90% of prisoners had Secondary education or less, versus 61% of the general population in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Although MHA declined to give certain information, it did provide the educational profile of the prison population when compared with the general population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It showed that in 2006, the percentage of the general population having Secondary education or less was 61%, but this was the profile of nearly 90% of the prison population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Conversely, the higher educated with more than Secondary education made up nearly 40% of the general population, but only 10% of the prison population.

sections.label: Bail release rates study
sections.summary: A 2005 study found only 42.7% of accused persons offered bail by the Subordinate Courts in 2004 were bailed out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a 2005 study by an Assistant Registrar of the Supreme Court, she found that in 2004, out of all accused persons offered bail by the Subordinate Courts, only 42.7% were bailed out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In other words, the majority of persons considered suitable for release before trial remained locked up.

sections.label: Money bail affects the poor
sections.summary: Heavy reliance on money bail disproportionately affects the poor, with HDB rental residents facing bail above $10,000 for non-violent regulatory offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The heavy reliance on money bail has disproportionate effects on the poor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have come across residents living in HDB rental flats who had bail set at above $10,000 for numerous charges of non-violent, regulatory offences like parking and ERP violations.

sections.label: Bail Court established in 2007
sections.summary: A Bail Court was established in 2007 to achieve consistency in bail decisions, reduce bail amounts and remand time, and handle reviews expeditiously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A Bail Court had been established in 2007 with the aim of achieving consistency in bail decisions and, where possible, to reduce bail amounts, reduce time spent in remand and ensure that review applications were dealt with expeditiously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In his reply in 2008, the Minister said that the Bail Court had reduced or varied the terms of bail in 30% of the cases referred to it.

sections.label: Blood samples from foreign workers
sections.summary: Blood samples were taken from 200 foreign workers at nearby construction sites in a questionable exercise of power.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a questionable exercise of power, blood samples were taken from 200 foreign workers at nearby construction sites.

sections.label: Composition notices with two deadlines
sections.summary: Some agencies have started issuing composition notices with two deadlines, the second offering a composition amount about $20 higher.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lately, I have noticed that some agencies have started issuing composition notices with two deadlines – one offering the usual composition amount and a second deadline offering a composition amount that is higher by about $20.

sections.label: Auto-tracking of Court fine instalments
sections.summary: The State Courts has an auto-tracking system for instalment payment of Court fines, with AXS kiosks showing instalment due dates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The State Courts already has a successful auto-tracking system for instalment payment of Court fines, with AXS kiosks showing the due dates for instalments.

sections.label: Recording statements in suspect's language
sections.summary: Law enforcement agencies should facilitate recording of statements in the suspect's language of choice to save time and expense at trial.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To save time and expense at the trial, law enforcement agencies should facilitate the recording of statements in the suspect's language of choice.

sections.label: Recording statements in official languages
sections.summary: The speaker suggests recording statements in Malay, Chinese and Tamil and expanding video or audio recording beyond serious sexual crime cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the very least, I suggest that the recording of statements should be facilitated in our other official languages of Malay, Chinese and Tamil.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, the use of video recording or audio recording of statements should be expanded to more cases than the current practice of using them for serious sexual crime only and other limited cases.

sections.label: UN Declaration on crime victims
sections.summary: In 1985 the UN General Assembly issued a Declaration urging governments to inform crime victims, consider their views, treat them fairly and provide compensation mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirty-five years ago, in 1985, the United Nations General Assembly issued a Declaration of Basic Principles of Justice for Victims of Crime and Abuse of Power.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Declaration, governments were urged to ensure that crime victims were informed of their role and the progress of their cases, that their views be considered at appropriate stages of the case, that they overall be treated fairly and that there be appropriate mechanisms for them to obtain compensation in criminal cases.

sections.label: Resident hit at junction
sections.summary: A resident was knocked down by a car while crossing at a junction with the green man sign in her favour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In one case, a resident was knocked down by a car while crossing the road at a junction with the green man sign in her favour.

sections.label: Driver charged, fined, suspended
sections.summary: After investigations, the Police told her the driver was charged with careless driving and was fined $2,000 and suspended for a few months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After investigations were concluded, she was shocked to receive a letter from the Police telling her that the driver had been charged with careless driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The family was also told that he had been fined $2,000 and suspended from driving for a few months.

sections.label: Police closed case letter
sections.summary: After investigations, she received a curt letter saying the Police had consulted the Attorney-General's Chambers and decided no further action would be taken.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After Police investigations, she received a curt letter stating that the Police had consulted the Attorney-General's Chambers and decided that no further action would be taken and the case would be closed.

sections.label: Review justice for victims
sections.summary: The speaker says crime victims deserve justice and respect and that the justice system should be reviewed from victims' perspective using the UN Declaration as a guide.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We need to remember that crime victims deserve justice and deserve to be treated with respect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should review our justice system from the crime victims' perspective and see how it can be improved using the UN's Declaration as a guide.

sections.label: Government jurisdiction concerns and suggestions
sections.summary: The Government should assess whether concerns and suggestions in its sole jurisdiction are valid and act, including on composition fines, reform, enforcement practices and crime victims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In the areas that are within the Government's sole jurisdiction, the Government should objectively assess whether there is validity in our concerns and suggestions and, if so, take action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: From my speech, these low-hanging fruit include composition fines, real reform, various law enforcement practices, such as statement-recording and training and the position of crime victims.

sections.label: Proposed Constitutional Commission
sections.summary: A Constitutional Commission headed by a Supreme Court Judge is suggested, including members with criminology or sociology expertise and experience with the poor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: For such issues, we suggest the setting up of a Constitutional Commission headed by a Supreme Court Judge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The Commission should include members with expertise in criminology or sociology and strong personal experience working with the poor.

sections.label: Excellent justice system for all
sections.summary: Singapore aims for excellence and should aim for an excellent justice system that works for everyone regardless of means or social status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Singapore regularly aims for excellence in its endeavours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: We should aim for an excellent justice system too, one that works for everyone, regardless of means or social status.

sections.label: Liyani acquittal and legal system
sections.summary: The acquittal judgment in Liyani's case pointed out the need to strengthen the pillars through a very sound legal system.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In recent years, the acquittal judgment that was passed in Liyani's case has already pointed out the need for us to strengthen the pillars only through a very sound legal system.

sections.label: Vulnerable accused without legal representation
sections.summary: Those without legal representation, resources or knowledge of the legal system may own up to charges, face delays and discrimination, unlike Prosecutors.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Without any legal representation – if our country faces any obstacles for the vulnerable, especially those without the resources to find our own legal representation, without any knowledge of the legal system, then when they are charged, they will become very nervous and they will just own up to all the charges put across to them and what is worse is that even if they have the ability to seek justice, then simply because they were not allowed, they do not have the ability to pay for the bill, therefore their are case is delayed and, therefore, they are discriminated by their own friends and family.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In contrast to the Prosecutors, these defence lawyers have no right to hold onto the evidence or to force certain witnesses to give their evidence.

sections.label: Fines, instalments and official languages
sections.summary: Sylvia Lim mentioned paying fines and instalments and allowing the accused to use Malay, Tamil and Chinese for their own written statement.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, Sylvia Lim also mentioned about the possibility of paying fines and instalment and for bill, to allow the accused to also be able to adopt the other official languages of Singapore, Malay, Tamil and Chinese to offer their own written statement.

sections.label: Unrepresented accused persons in courts
sections.summary: Defence counsel are a pillar of justice, yet about 40% of accused persons who claimed trial appeared unrepresented at State Courts pretrial stages.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: (In English): As I have mentioned earlier, one of the pillars, the house of justice, represents defence counsel who represent persons who are accused of crimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given the crucial role of defence counsel, it is disquieting to see that a significant proportion of accused persons still appear before the Courts unrepresented, with approximately 40% of accused persons who claimed trial appearing unrepresented at the State Courts during pretrial stages.

sections.label: Criminal Legal Aid Scheme criteria
sections.summary: CLAS, run by the Law Society and funded by MinLaw, may grant legal aid for non-capital offences subject to income, capital and merits tests.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For non-capital offences, the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme or CLAS administered by the Law Society of Singapore and also funded by the MinLaw provides accused persons with a disposable income of not more than $10,000 per annum and disposable capital of not more than $10,000 may be granted legal aid, subject to an additional merits test.

sections.label: State legal aid obligations
sections.summary: The state is obliged to provide legal aid to persons with intellectual and mental disabilities, those facing six months or more in prison, and those meeting a financial threshold.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The state is also obliged to provide legal aid to persons with intellectual and mental disabilities, persons who face a potential prison sentence of six months or more, and persons who meet a financial threshold.

sections.label: Enacting Legal Aid and Advice Ordinance
sections.summary: The speaker suggests enacting the original Legal Aid and Advice Ordinance, first sought after David Marshall's 1955 call, for equal access to justice.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given all these, perhaps it is now time for us to enact the provisions of the original Legal Aid and Advice Ordinance which were first introduced after David Marshall in 1955 called for a statutory requirement for the provision of legal aid, including criminal matters, to the indigent, for everyone in Singapore to have equal access to the justice system rather than rely on having these resources provided on a voluntary basis by the profession.

sections.label: Duty lawyers and lawyer access
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering Criminal Procedure Code amendments, a fixed time for access to a lawyer, and rostering state-funded police station or Court duty lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It should also look into considering amendments to the Criminal Procedure Code and whether there should be a fixed time within which an accused person will be permitted access to a lawyer.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can explore having a system of rostering state-funded police station or Court duty lawyers, enabling a person arrested on suspicion of a criminal offence to consult with a lawyer after arrest or allow an accused person to be represented by a lawyer at a Court on their first appearance if they have not or have not been able to contact their lawyer.

sections.label: Compensation for wrongful conviction
sections.summary: Section 359(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code allows acquitted persons compensation up to $10,000 if the prosecution was frivolous or vexatious, and the speaker compares this with UK schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, section 359(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code allows for the acquitted person to be compensated a sum not exceeding $10,000, provided that the Court is satisfied that the prosecution was frivolous or vexatious.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Genuine mistakes do happen and, given that cases can last a long time, such as the case of Chibuike being a recent one where the accused was in remand for nine long years after his arrest for drug trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This contrasts against schemes in other jurisdictions, such as the United Kingdom where section 133 of the Criminal Justice Act 1998 states that "The state shall pay compensation for the miscarriage of justice to the person who has been convicted, suffered punishment and subsequently had his conviction reserved or pardoned on the ground of a newly-discovered fact that shows that there was a miscarriage of justice." The legislation is very specific about the circumstances which make such persons eligible for compensation, and the amount of compensation depends on the seriousness of the offence of which the person was convicted or accused, the severity of the punishment suffered, the conduct of investigation and prosecution of the offence and any other convictions of that person.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I realise that this is a complex issue which requires a balance in ensuring that genuine victims of miscarriages of justice are compensated against being so generous as to possibly introduce a chill factor in carrying out prosecutions that may hamper the efficient administration of justice for crimes committed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, note that, in the UK, there were only 14 successful cases between 2010 and 2013 out of a total of 398 applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Be that as it may, serious consideration of our existing scheme is still warranted to ensure that wrongly convicted persons may be adequately compensated in what is, after all, a serious deprivation both financially and to their personal liberty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, the High Court ruled that the Liew family may have ulterior motives, and wrongly accused their former maid Liyani of stealing.

sections.label: Police lapse and AGC proceedings
sections.summary: The Minister said police committed a lapse handling exhibits, and AGC began legal and disciplinary proceedings over prosecutors' handling of the DVD player.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, as for the police, the Minister was of the view that the police did commit a lapse in handling the exhibits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Second, in response to the handling of the DVD player by the prosecutors, AGC has also initiated relevant legal and disciplinary proceedings.

sections.label: Foreign domestic workers arrested for theft
sections.summary: In 2016, 245 foreign domestic workers were arrested for theft, about 0.1% of all such workers, and 188 were not charged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to figures in the Ministerial Statement, in 2016, 245 foreign domestic workers were arrested for theft, about 0.1% of all domestic workers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Of the 245 foreign domestic workers arrested by the police, 188, or nearly 80 per cent, were not charged.

sections.label: Police evidence lapses due to workload
sections.summary: The Minister said police lapses in handling evidence involved manpower and workload, not professional conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: As pointed out by the Minister in his statement, there were lapses on the police when handling the evidence this time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In fact, it has to do with manpower and workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In other words, this is not a question of professional conduct.

sections.label: Proper channels and learning from case
sections.summary: Unlike Justice Bao legends, Singapore has legal aid and the Yellow Ribbon Project, and authorities will learn from this painful experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to legends, when people wanted to seek redress from Justice Bao, they could stop him on the road, or drum up their grievances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But in our country, we have proper channels such as legal aid for civil cases and criminal cases, and the Yellow Ribbon Project to help former convicts to reintegrate into society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: After this case, I am sure the authorities will learn from this painful experience and draw lessons from it.

sections.label: Singapore's low crime rate
sections.summary: Singapore's crime rate is one of the lowest in the world despite being close to the drug trade's golden triangle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore's crime rate is one of the lowest in the world and this is despite the fact that we are sitting close to the "golden triangle" for the drug trade.

sections.label: Low recidivism for non-drug crimes
sections.summary: Singapore's recidivism rate is also low, especially for those whose crimes are not drug-related.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our rate of recidivism is also low, especially for those whose crimes are not drug-related.

sections.label: Criminal disclosure requirements amended 2010
sections.summary: The 2010 amended criminal disclosure requirements required the prosecution to disclose a case summary, exhibit list and Police statements before the hearing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The criminal disclosure requirements that were amended in 2010 required the prosecution to disclose a summary of their case, a list of exhibits the witnesses would rely on, including Police statements prior to the hearing.

sections.label: 2018 broadening of covered offences
sections.summary: In 2018, further amendments broadened the list of offences covered by these procedures to include Moneylenders Act and Prevention of Corruption Act offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2018, following further amendments, the list of offences covered by these procedures were broadened to include offences under the Moneylenders Act and the Prevention of Corruption Act.

sections.label: Victim compensation in all cases
sections.summary: The 2010 reforms required the Courts to consider victim compensation in all cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The 2010 reforms required the Courts to consider victim compensation in all cases.

sections.label: 2010 alternatives to imprisonment
sections.summary: In 2010, a wide range of alternatives was introduced, including short detention orders, day reporting orders, mandatory treatment orders, community service orders and community work orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2010, a wide range of alternatives was introduced, including short detention orders, day reporting orders, mandatory treatment orders, community service orders and community work orders.

sections.label: Video recording and Appropriate Adult Scheme
sections.summary: In 2018 video recording of interviews was introduced, and in 2013 the Appropriate Adult Scheme was piloted for suspects with autism, mental health conditions and intellectual disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2018, another significant step was the introduction of video recording of interviews because what took place when police statements were recorded started becoming more contentious as these were challenged in trial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2013, the Appropriate Adult Scheme was piloted for suspects with autism spectrum disorder, mental health conditions and intellectual disabilities.

sections.label: LASCO legal representation for capital crimes
sections.summary: The Supreme Court's Legal Assistance Scheme for Capital Offences, or LASCO, provides everyone accused of capital crimes with legal representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Supreme Court's Legal Assistance Scheme for Capital Offences, or LASCO, provides everyone accused of capital crimes with legal representation.

sections.label: Public defender's office support
sections.summary: The speaker supports a public defender's office to institutionalise lawyers defending victims needing earlier access, but lacks a straightforward answer on resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If resources permit, and as was clear from the question I raised earlier, it would be helpful if more people are given access to legal counsel and possibly at an earlier stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I do not have a straightforward answer to this because of the difficult question of how we are going to have adequate resources but I do support a public defender's office because this would at least institutionalise a group of lawyers who would be there to defend victims who need earlier access to lawyers.

sections.label: Civil legal aid access gaps
sections.summary: Many still do not qualify for civil legal aid or cannot find pro bono representation, and other lawyers' fees may be unaffordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Despite recent Government efforts to increase access for civil legal aid to the Legal Aid Bureau, many still do not qualify despite the exemplary efforts of many volunteer lawyers under the CLAS scheme and the Law Society pro bono schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Beyond the rendering of pro bono advice, many still cannot find someone to represent them in legal proceedings on pro bono basis or the quoted fees of other lawyers may be unaffordable.

sections.label: Parti Liyani appeal finding
sections.summary: The High Court Judge reviewing Parti Liyani's appeal found the State Courts trial Judge wrong in applying legal and evidential burdens of proof.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The hon High Court Judge reviewing Parti Liyani's appeal found that the trial Judge in the State Courts was wrong in applying the legal and evidential burdens of proof.

sections.label: State Courts Act Magistrate qualifications
sections.summary: Section 10(2) requires a Magistrate to be qualified for at least three years, but section 10(3) allows the Chief Justice to deem suitable those qualified one to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In a current version of section 10 of the State Courts Act, there is now the provision at section 10(2) requiring a Magistrate to be a qualified person for not less than three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However a person can still be a point under section 10(3) if the Chief Justice deems that he is suitable for the appointment even though he has been qualified for between one and three years.

sections.label: Greater specialisation among legal officers
sections.summary: In 2014 the Prime Minister announced greater specialisation among legal officers, with middle-rank officers posted to legal or judicial branches for some years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2014, the Prime Minister did announce the system of greater specialisation among legal officers so that at the middle ranks, officers can be posted either the legal or judicial branches and remain there for some years to hone their experience.

sections.label: Proposed specialised judicial track review
sections.summary: The speaker still thinks the proposed review should consider a more specialised judicial track at the State Court level and discontinuing inter-services posting with AGC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Law Minister share his views earlier with us on this issue during the Ministerial Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: But I am still of the view that it may still be worthwhile for the proposed review that we are proposing to still consider this issue of whether we should have a more specialised or dedicated judicial track at the State Court level, encompassing Magistrates and District Judges, and discontinuing inter-services posting or rotation with other branches of the legal service, particularly with AGC.

sections.label: Separate judicial service proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests discarding the current nomenclature and having a dedicated judicial service set apart from the legal service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Up till now, judicial officers or AGC staff often regard themselves as working for the legal service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: It is perhaps time to discard this nomenclature and have a dedicated judicial service set apart from the rest of the legal service.

sections.label: Judicial College training and research
sections.summary: The Judicial College runs courses on public engagement and has embarked on research on litigants-in-person and access to justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In addition to the hard skills in law administration, there are courses focused on enhancing the experience of the public, such as effective engagement of litigants who are unrepresented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I also note from its Annual Report that the Judicial College has embarked on forthcoming research on litigants-in-person and access to justice in an adversarial system, a topic which is of high importance.

sections.label: Resources and literacy gaps
sections.summary: An example shows a person cannot distinguish the Prosecutor's authorities or rebut mistakes, exemplifying resources and literacy gaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: He cannot distinguish the authorities submitted by the Prosecutor and would not even be able to rebut the Prosecutor if there is any mistake in applying the authorities to the facts of the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This common example exemplifies both the resources gap and the literacy gap which the Chief Justice has talked about.

sections.label: Training State Courts Judges
sections.summary: The speaker exhorts the Singapore Judicial College to continue enhancing training for State Courts Judges to reduce the physical gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A local Singapore case involving a previous Chief Justice was, in fact sight, cited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Indeed, I would exhort the Singapore Judicial College to continue to enhance its training for Judges in the State Courts in the areas I have talked about, which in my respectful view, will certainly help to reduce any physical gap, using the term as mentioned by the Chief Justice, and to further enhance our justice system.

sections.label: Codifying prosecution disclosure duties
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that the Prosecution's common law disclosure obligations be codified in the Criminal Procedure Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One focuses on fairness and the other focuses on independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I will first speak on the Prosecution's duty of disclosure and propose that its common law disclosure obligations be codified in the Criminal Procedure Code or CPC.

sections.label: Kadar disclosure ruling
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal in Kadar ruled the prosecution must disclose credible and relevant unused material favourable to the defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I would say that we were still in some shadows as the CPC amendments did not require the prosecution to disclose material such as witnesses' statements that might help the defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This changed in 2011 with the Court of Appeal's judgment in Muhammad bin Kadar and another versus Public Prosecutor – hereinafter, referred to as Kadar – where the Court ruled that the prosecution must disclose to the defence any credible and relevant unused material that would be favourable to the defence's case.

sections.label: Court of Appeal disclosure ruling
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal ruled the prosecution withheld documents showing inconsistencies, prejudicing Dr Wee, and reminded the prosecution of its duty of fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In its judgment released in June this year, the Court of Appeal ruled that the prosecution did not make available to the defence documents that would have established clear and material inconsistencies in the prosecution's evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal decided that the delay in disclosing one document in particular, prejudiced Dr Wee, even as the prosecution ran the argument that that document was actually irrelevant to the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Court reminded the prosecution of its overarching duty of fairness, in addition to a duty to the Court and the public, to ensure that only the guilty are convicted.

sections.label: Nabill expands Kadar disclosure obligations
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal in Nabill expanded Kadar disclosure obligations, ruling all material witnesses' statements, including neutral or adverse ones, be released routinely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, the Court of Appeal's decision in Muhammad Nabill bin Mohd Fuad versus Public Prosecutor, also released this year, has expanded the Kadar disclosure obligations even further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, Kadar did not require the release of statements that were neutral or adverse to the defence, but the Court in Nabill ruled that as the statements of material witnesses would in most cases be limited, and that all statements including those neutral or adverse to the defence should be released to the defence as a matter of routine.

sections.label: Codifying prosecution disclosure obligations
sections.summary: The prosecution accepted it breached Kadar and Nabill disclosure obligations, and the speaker suggested codifying these obligations in the Criminal Procedure Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At this hearing, the prosecution also accepted there had been a breach of its disclosure obligations under Kadar and Nabill, and that the trial judge had erred in concluding that a statement in question was not liable to be disclosed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These cases bring me to my suggestion to this House that the prosecution's disclosure obligations should be codified in the Criminal Procedure Code.

sections.label: Legislating against inadvertent non-disclosure
sections.summary: The speaker said Parliament must legislate forthwith because of the prospect of inadvertent non-disclosure causing future miscarriages of justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In my view, Mr Speaker, it is precisely because of the very prospect of inadvertent non-disclosure that Parliament has to legislate forthwith to prevent possible future miscarriages of justice because of non-disclosure.

sections.label: Defence still faces problem
sections.summary: The speaker stated that even when the prosecution discloses helpful witness statements, the defence still has a problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The fact today is that even if the prosecution discloses to the defence witnesses statements that could help the accused person's case, the defence still has a problem.

sections.label: Interviewing witnesses in police station
sections.summary: The speaker suggested defence counsel be given the option to interview witnesses helpful to the defence in a police station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To achieve greater fairness before trial, my suggestion is that arrangements should be made for defence counsel to be given the option to interview witnesses, whose statements are helpful to the defence, in a police station.

sections.label: Workers' Party calls AG split
sections.summary: The Workers' Party calls on the Government to split the Attorney-General's office into public prosecutor and Government legal advisor roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order that there be greater independence in the criminal justice system that can be readily seen by the public, the Workers' Party calls upon the Government to split the office of the Attorney-General or AG into two roles of the public prosecutor and the Government's legal advisor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party called for the splitting of roles of the AG in our 2020 election Manifesto.

sections.label: AG prosecution discretion
sections.summary: The Attorney-General has absolute discretion over whether and whom to prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Two, the AG has absolute discretion as to whether and who to prosecute.

sections.label: Dual roles conflict of interest
sections.summary: The AG as public prosecutor must prosecute without fear or favour, and the duality of roles creates potential conflict of interest and abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the public prosecutor, the AG represents the public and must prosecute without fear or favour, even if it means damaging the reputation of the government of the day, or prosecuting Ministers or even the Prime Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This duality of roles in one person brings with it a potential conflict of interest for the AG which can create potential for abuse.

sections.label: Split advisor and prosecutor roles
sections.summary: The first change is to split the role of Government legal advisor from the role of public prosecutor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first and most obvious change is to split the role of Government legal advisor from the role of public prosecutor.

sections.label: Fixed term for public prosecutor
sections.summary: The second suggestion is for the public prosecutor to be appointed for a fixed term of relatively significant length.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second suggestion is for the public prosecutor to be appointed for a fixed term of a relatively significant length.

sections.label: Five-year term, no ex-MP
sections.summary: The Workers' Party is open to a five-year term, and the third suggestion is to eschew appointing an ex-Member of Parliament as public prosecutor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party is open to this idea of a five-year term as we believe it not only promotes stability, but also independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The third suggestion is for the system to eschew to the appointment of an ex-Member of Parliament as public prosecutor.

sections.label: Attorney-General recusal in Parti Liyani case
sections.summary: The Attorney-General's Chambers stated that Attorney-General Lucien Wong was not involved in prosecutorial decisions on Ms Parti Liyani and would recuse himself from the case review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And insofar, as public confidence and trust is concerned, perception is highly significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is noteworthy that the Attorney-General's Chambers made it a point to release a statement that the Attorney-General, Mr Lucien Wong was not involved in any prosecutorial decisions regarding Ms Parti Liyani, and that he would recuse himself from the review of the case.

sections.label: Sylvia Lim on splitting Attorney-General roles
sections.summary: Ms Sylvia Lim raised splitting the Attorney-General's roles in February 2020, and the reply was that most of the public has confidence in the justice system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim raised the splitting of the roles of the Attorney-General at the Committee of Supply Debate for the Attorney-General's Chambers in February 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Essentially, his reply was that a large proportion of the public has confidence in our justice system; our system is working well, and it has sufficient safeguards.

sections.label: Workers' Party on splitting Attorney-General roles
sections.summary: The Workers' Party says amending the Constitution involves trade-offs, but argues there are no negative trade-offs in splitting the Attorney-General's roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party understands that policy-making and in this case, amending the Constitution often involves trade-offs and crucially an eye into the future about how a law or policy will serve situations that had not been originally envisaged and can last the test of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I would argue that there are no negative trade-offs in splitting the roles of the Attorney-General into the public prosecutor and the Government's legal advisor.

sections.label: Support for Constitutional Commission review
sections.summary: The speaker says the current structure is weak, sees no robust reasons for one person holding all Attorney-General roles, and supports review by a Constitutional Commission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is weakness in the current structure and improvements should be made to strengthen the system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are also no robust reasons for all the AGs' roles to be held by one person and to that end, I support Ms Sylvia Lim's call for this issue of the splitting of the Attorney General's roles to be reviewed by a Constitutional Commission.

sections.label: Support for Motion and Parti Liyani inquiry
sections.summary: The speaker supports Ms Sylvia Lim's Motion and calls for an open and independent inquiry into Parti Liyani's case, citing lapses in the Police, prosecution and State Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If a future occupant of that house uses it in a way that it was not meant to be used, for example, like for commercial storage or is a restaurant, the foundations may give way, harming all the occupants of the house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is no reason why we cannot fix the foundations or at the very least strengthen it now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In doing so, we can move the needle on justice and independence in our legal system and in doing so leave a more secure justice system that reinforces the rule of law in Singapore for our next generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I support the Motion in the name of Ms Sylvia Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my exchanges with the Minister for Home Affairs just now, I would like to state my case again for an open and independent inquiry into Parti Liyani's case for further consideration by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We think that the wide implications of the lapses in the criminal justice system in the Parti Liyani case warrant an open and independent inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I do not think it is unfair to say that there were lapses in all three major institutions of our criminal justice system – the Police, the prosecution and the State Courts.

sections.label: Independent inquiry into criminal justice process
sections.summary: An independent inquiry could examine the entire criminal justice process across the three major institutions to identify systemic problems for improvement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: An independent inquiry would be able to examine the entire criminal justice process across all the three major institutions to ensure that systemic problems, where identified, are acknowledged by the various institutions and considered for improvement to the system.

sections.label: Wealth gap and inquiry
sections.summary: It states that privilege and entitlement divides could cause revolt, and that an independent public inquiry would show justice is done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is the reality of a capitalist society like Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But they will revolt if, on top of this wealth gap, there is a privilege and entitlement divide that separates the elites from the masses.” Convening an independent inquiry with hearings that are open to the public, or live-streamed, would go a long way to show our citizens that justice is being done.

sections.label: Independent inquiry broadcast live
sections.summary: It says an independent committee of inquiry with live-broadcast proceedings would prove the country upholds justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The best way to dispel any doubt is to set up independent committee of inquiry and broadcast the proceedings live.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will prove to our people that our country will uphold justice.

sections.label: Workers' Party ombudsman proposals
sections.summary: The Workers' Party advocated an independent ombudsman in its 2015 and 2020 manifestos, and a Police Complaints Commission in 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party has advocated for setting up the office of an independent ombudsman in our GE 2015 and 2020 manifestos.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In its GE 2011 Manifesto, the Workers' Party proposed the establishment of an independent Police Complaints Commission for some of the same reasons.

sections.label: 1966 Wee Chong Jin Commission
sections.summary: The 1966 Wee Chong Jin Constitutional Commission recommended an ombudsman as an independent check on public sector acts and decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The 1966 Wee Chong Jin Constitutional Commission recommended instituting an ombudsman to ensure an independent check on the acts and decisions of the public sector, apart from the principle of Ministerial responsibility.

sections.label: Davinder Singh and Shanmugam ombudsman calls
sections.summary: In 1990 Davinder Singh and in 1994 K Shanmugam called in Parliament for an ombudsman to give citizens a remedy for grievances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 1990, then Member of Parliament Mr Davinder Singh called for the establishment of the ombudsman, noting that, and I quote, "it is in our interest that we develop a system of accountability, a system which will assure the man in the street that if he has a grievance, he can take it up to a person or a body who has a right or has a power to look into it, look into the files of the Ministry, if necessary, or bring a complaint of shoddy treatment up to the superiors".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 1994, as has been alluded to earlier today, then backbencher and current Law Minister Mr K Shanmugam also raised it in Parliament, suggesting that an ombudsman, and I quote, "might actually help retain the confidence of people in the system, to have an intermediate institution which can provide for a quick and effective remedy and reserving the final appeal to the minister for extreme cases".

sections.label: OECD ombudsman working paper
sections.summary: A 2018 OECD working paper said almost 30% of governments included ombudsman offices, most handling complaints against public administration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2018 OECD working paper noted that almost 30% of governments have included independent institutions like ombudsman offices to foster a more "open state" which OECD recommendation on the council open government defines as and I quote, "When the executive legislature judiciary independent public institutions and all levels of government recognising the respective roles, prerogatives and overall independence according to their existing legal and institutional frameworks collaborate, exploit synergies and share good practises and lessons learnt among themselves and with other stakeholders to promote transparency, integrity, accountability and stakeholder participation and support of democracy and inclusive growth." Notably, 96% of the ombudsman institutions studied in this report focus on complaints against the public administration and 67% also conduct mediation of such complaints between citizens and the public administration.

sections.label: Hong Kong Ombudsman powers
sections.summary: The Hong Kong Ombudsman can investigate maladministration complaints, access-to-information non-compliance, and initiate direct investigations of wide public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Hong Kong Ombudsman has powers to: firstly, investigate complaints from aggrieved persons about maladministration; secondly investigate complaints against government departments and agencies for non-compliance with a code of access to information; and thirdly, initiate direct investigation into issues of potentially wide public interest and concern.

sections.label: Proposed Singapore independent ombudsman
sections.summary: The Ombudsman reports to Parliament on AFP complaint handling, and an independent ombudsman office is proposed for external review consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ombudsman reports to Parliament, at least annually, on the comprehensiveness and adequacy of the AFP's complaint handling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have argued for the creation of an office of independent ombudsman in Singapore to investigate complaints against public servants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We propose submitting the idea of creating such an office as an item to be considered in the external review described by my Party Chair and Member of Parliament, Ms Sylvia Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The review process could consider the role such an ombudsman could play in our current eco-system of laws, regulations and practices, in the context of the questions raised by the Parti Liyani's case and taking into consideration and useful lessons from the study of the operating model for an ombudsman in force at other jurisdictions.

sections.label: Government rejection of ombudsman
sections.summary: Singapore Government rejection of an ombudsman appears premised on existing mechanisms being sufficient for public feedback, trust and institutional integrity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, the Singapore Government rejection of the notion of an ombudsman seems to be premised on the fact that there are sufficient mechanisms already in place to receive public feedback, safeguard public trust and maintain the integrity of public institutions.

sections.label: Public Service Commission limits
sections.summary: The Public Service Commission is not an investigative body and lacks resources and expertise to approximate an ombudsman office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we have the Public Service Commission or PSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the PSC is not an investigative body per se and does not possess the resources and expertise to look into complaints against the Public Service to approximate what we see in the office of the ombudsman in, say, Hong Kong and Australia.

sections.label: Two AGO Special Audits
sections.summary: A 2016 Parliamentary reply stated only two AGO Special Audits were ordered in 20 years, on 1996 healthcare subsidies and 2014 Aljunied-Hougang-Punggol East Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2016, I obtained a Parliamentary reply to the effect that there have only been two AGO Special Audits ordered by the Government in the past 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The first related to claims made by Opposition Members of Parliament in Parliament about healthcare subsidies in 1996.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second was a request audit of the Workers' Party left Aljunied-Hougang-Punggol East Town Council in 2014.

sections.label: Independent avenue of redress
sections.summary: An independent avenue of redress would strengthen public confidence and advance the Motion's call for accessible justice for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: In doing so, it would strengthen public confidence in the state among our citizens since they would know that there is an independent avenue of redress accessible to the ordinary citizen who cannot afford costly legal action against the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Such a move would be a significant step towards achieving what this Motion today calls for, making justice accessible to all.

sections.label: Police and AGC case preparation
sections.summary: The investigation found room for the police and AGC to improve case preparation, but no wrong-doing or influence was found.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The investigation showed that, amongst other things, indeed, there is room for the police and the Attorney-General's Chamber to improve the process of preparing the case for trial.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, the Police should not have taken so long to take a record of the things that were said to be stolen after the police report was made.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This shortcoming was acknowledged and assurance was given that this matter will be given attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, there was no finding of any wrong-doing or influence over the police or AGC.

sections.label: Criminal cases and prosecutions in 2019
sections.summary: In 2019, 35,209 criminal cases were recorded, with prosecutors handling over 500 trial cases and 6,189 guilty plea cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2019, there were 35,209 criminal cases recorded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the same year, the prosecutors dealt with more than 500 trial cases and 6,189 cases where the accused pleaded guilty.

sections.label: Access to justice and legal aid
sections.summary: The speaker describes access to justice and their time on the Legal Aid Bureau panel helping with divorce cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This what is talked about when we discuss access to justice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I was on the panel of the Legal Aid Bureau for a while and managed to help with a few divorce cases for those who could not afford legal costs.

sections.label: Uncontested divorces and assistance schemes
sections.summary: Uncontested divorces can be processed more easily at the Family Justice Courts, with room to assist those not meeting existing scheme criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: For example, uncontested divorces can be processed more easily at the Family Justice Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, there is room to increase assistance given to those who may not meet the criteria for existing schemes.

sections.label: Workplace discrimination complaint channel
sections.summary: For workplace discrimination, there is a channel to make a complaint and ask for justice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: If there is an issue of discrimination at the workplace, for example, there is a channel to make a complaint and ask for justice.

sections.label: Preserving confidence in justice system
sections.summary: It is important to preserve society's and the world's confidence in the transparency and integrity of the justice system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: While we try to find the shortcomings and improve our justice system, it is important to preserve our society’s and the world’s confidence in the transparency and integrity of our system.

sections.label: CLAS coverage of households
sections.summary: CLAS covers 25% of resident households, or is intended to.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As I said, CLAS covers 25% of resident households or is intended to.

sections.label: Criminal legal aid expenditure increase
sections.summary: Government expenditure on criminal legal aid increased by 50% from 2015 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Government expenditure on criminal legal aid has seen a 50% increase from 2015 to 2019.

sections.label: Cost of defence to taxpayers
sections.summary: The cost to taxpayers of his defence was around $2.3 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Cost to taxpayers of his defence was around $2.3 million.

sections.label: Total cost rise
sections.summary: The total cost rose by 62%, from $101 million in 2006 and 2007 to $164 million in 2018 and 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The total cost rising by 62% from $101 million in 2006 and 2007 to $164 million in 2018 and 2019.

sections.label: Bar relationship and public defender's office
sections.summary: The relationship with the bar is constructive, the bar does pro bono through CLAS, and a sustainable public defender's office is being considered.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We, thankfully, have a relationship with a bar which is more constructive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: They do pro bono through CLAS but I have said that we are now considering how we can set up a public defender's office which would be sustainable.

sections.label: Remand releases with e-tagging
sections.summary: Since 2018 more remanded persons are released on reduced bail with e-tagging; over 180 were released between January and July, and the CPC was amended in 2018 to provide for e-tagging.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Since 2018, increasing number of persons in remand are being released on a reduced bail with e-tagging – because we can use technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Between January and July, more than 180 accused persons have been released on reduced bail with e-tagging.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In 2018, I think some Members will recall that the Criminal Procedure Code or CPC was amended to specifically provide for e-tagging and the Police are generally prepared to consider allowing personal bonds in more cases.

sections.label: Police IO legal training
sections.summary: Police officers in the IO role take legal modules on investigative powers, charges, the Evidence Act and trial preparation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Police officers who take on the IO role do take some legal modules on investigative powers, drafting of charges and statement of facts, to understand the Evidence Act, the burden of proof, presumptions, on general law, on general training for trial preparation.

sections.label: Police IO disciplinary inquiry
sections.summary: The specific Police IO in Ms Liyani's case will face a disciplinary inquiry, and the speaker says people are not scape-goated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Ms Lim said something which I heartily agree with – that the specific Police IO in Ms Liyani's case does not become a scape-goat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I will start out by saying that we do not scape-goat people, but when I come to the Parliament, I cannot shy away from saying what has happened.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I cannot shy away from saying that unfortunately – I did say "unfortunately" – he will have to face disciplinary inquiry.

sections.label: Instalment payments on fines
sections.summary: The speaker directed the Police to consider areas for possible instalment payments on fines, without setting up another mechanism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We do not want to go down the route of setting up another mechanism, more resources to go and check that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But subject to that, I have given directions earlier this year to the Police to consider in which areas we can go, for possibility of instalment payments on fines.

sections.label: Guidance programme completion rates
sections.summary: Over the past four years there were four to five hundred guidance programme cases a year, with completion rates of about 80% to 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In the past four years, four to five hundred guidance programmes cases a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Completion rate has been about 80% to 90%.

sections.label: Compensation for miscarriage of justice
sections.summary: The speaker says that in principle, compensation ought to be paid if a case is vexatious and should never have been brought.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Ms He Ting Ru also talked about compensation for miscarriage of justice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I think in principle, if it is a vexatious case, if it should never have been brought, compensation ought to be paid.

sections.label: Magistrates and District Judges tenure
sections.summary: One year for Magistrates and three for District Judges is possible only if the Chief Justice finds the person suitable; otherwise normal terms are three and seven years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The point he made about one year for Magistrates and three years for District Judges, or DJs – that is only possible when the Chief Justice is of the opinion that the person is suitable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Otherwise, the normal process is three years for Magistrates and seven years for District Judges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In the State Courts today, we have 55 Judicial Officers who hear criminal cases.

sections.label: Disclosure requirements in statute
sections.summary: The speaker says setting out disclosure requirements in statute has been discussed internally since early this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Looking at setting out the disclosure requirements in statute, I am happy to tell him that, knowing that he is going to raise it today, we have been discussing it since early this year, internally.

sections.label: 2018 amendment on compensation reasons
sections.summary: In 2018 the law was amended so Courts must give reasons when compensation is not awarded where they have power to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, I actually decided that we had to go further.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, in 2018, the law was further amended and now, the Courts are required to give reasons if compensation is not awarded, where it has the power to do so.

sections.label: Duties of Members of Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker says MPs must apply their minds to feedback and arguments, and asks which part requires further inquiry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: You see, the duties of Members of Parliament, is not to come and repeat whatever is outside but to apply our mind, take whatever feedback there is, crystallise it, apply it to the facts, listen to the arguments on the other side, and then say, “Yes, I see all these; now, I will tell you what it is.” Because if you ask for a Commission of Inquiry, it is because you are not happy with something.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: You feel that there is a reasonable basis for having an inquiry into something.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, you need to tell us which part of this requires further inquiry.

sections.label: Prepared to have commission of inquiry
sections.summary: The speaker says they are prepared to have a commission of inquiry and that officers and the supervisor will face disciplinary inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Can you just help me because I have said we are happy to have – not happy – but we are prepared to have a commission of inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I did say the officers involved will face Police disciplinary inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of course, the supervisor will face the disciplinary inquiry, too, because of the five weeks.

sections.label: No basis for commission of inquiry
sections.summary: The speaker says there is no basis for a commission of inquiry against the Police or AGC, and no scapegoating of the young officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We do not want to make a scapegoat of this young officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There is no basis for a commission of inquiry against the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For AGC, there is no basis for doing a commission of inquiry because if you accept that the AGC officers' conduct will be dealt with by the Disciplinary Tribunal, they will go into it – why they did it, what they did – you have got your independent inquiry.

sections.label: Withdrawing proposal for inquiry
sections.summary: After the explanation, the speaker accepts a thorough investigation was done and withdraws the proposal for the inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We thought that the systemic faults alone are enough to be a basis for the inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But after your explanation, okay, we are prepared to accept that you have done a thorough investigation of the situation already, then we will withdraw our proposal for the inquiry.

sections.label: UK cautioned statement language provision
sections.summary: Speaker notes UK law records cautioned statements in the accused's language with later English translation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: He mentioned that while he does not think that that can be done, of course, he also said that I think the gold standard was video recording.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But I would also like to highlight that, in the UK, actually, they do have provision in their Police and Criminal Evidence Act that when an accused person wants to give a cautioned statement in a language other than English, that the police will record the statement in that language and later on an English translation will be provided.

sections.label: Recording statements other than English
sections.summary: Speaker acknowledges Police difficulties recording non-English statements and says other countries' models will be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think the recording of statements other than English, I know that Police have said, and I have a lot of sympathy for them that they have difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will look at the other countries and their models.

sections.label: 2018 victim compensation law amendment
sections.summary: In 2018 the law was amended so victims get compensation or Courts explain not giving it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In fact, in 2018, we amended the law so that victims would be given compensation or the Courts would have to explain why they are not being given compensation, if the Courts so choose not to.

sections.label: Legal assistance for the poor
sections.summary: Speaker agrees the poor should get legal assistance, finds the current system unsatisfactory, and warns against absolutist arguments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I believe like you that the poor should get legal assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have said that I do not find the current system satisfactory and that we have been discussing for some time how we can do it better.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I was addressing my remarks to some of the statements that you made but which were a little bit more absolutist – like this is a human right, this is cast in stone, it has to be done – and I pointed out that some of those may lead us into alleyways and byways which others have found themselves in and then we will get stuck in the weeds, and we would not be able to come back.

sections.label: Discharge for innocent foreign worker
sections.summary: A collective view found the man innocent, and as DPP the speaker sought a discharge amounting to acquittal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the end, we formed the collective view that, indeed, this man was innocent and had actually tried to break up the fight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I went to Court as a DPP to ask for a discharge amounting to an acquittal for the foreign worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: He was set free because of AGC's application for a discharge amounting to an acquittal.

sections.label: Video recording of accused statements
sections.summary: Over the years, video recording of statements by an accused has been introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, over the years, we have introduced the video recording of statements by an accused.

sections.label: Child victim identity and abuse offences
sections.summary: Provisions keep victims' identities confidential under the Children and Young Persons Act, and more offences cover child pornography and abuse content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We have introduced provisions to ensure that the victim's identity in an offence under the Children and Young Persons Act is held in strict confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And we have introduced more comprehensive offences to tackle the seriousness of child pornography and child abuse content.

sections.label: Mistreated maids hesitate to report
sections.summary: Mistreated or unpaid maids may hesitate to report to authorities, as with Miss Khalifa, abused six months by employers in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When faced with a situation where they are mistreated or denied their salaries, they may hesitate to make reports to the authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This was the case for Miss Khalifa, a maid from Indonesia who endured six months of horrific abuse at the hands of her employers in 2012.

sections.label: Maid abuse case timelines
sections.summary: For maid abuse cases going to Court, investigation takes at least a year and trial another year, besides appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For maid abuse cases that go to Court, the investigation alone can take at least a year while the trial could take another year, not to mention appeals.

sections.label: Special pass does not permit work
sections.summary: Victims assisting investigations get a special pass to remain in Singapore, but this grants no automatic right to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While victims for assisting in investigations are issued with a special pass to remain in Singapore, this does not grant them an automatic right to work.

sections.label: Compensation framework and language hurdles
sections.summary: Compensation is not guaranteed as perpetrators can avoid payment, and accused persons face the same language hurdles, as with Ms Parti Liyani.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While it is good that there is now a compensation framework for victims, this is not guaranteed as the perpetrator can escape payment of compensation by serving a jail term in lieu or claiming bankruptcy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The same language hurdles encountered by victims are also faced by those accused of crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This was the case for Ms Parti Liyani who, according to the High Court judgment, was interviewed for some of her statements by investigators in a mix of English and Bahasa Melayu while she spoke Bahasa Indonesia.

sections.label: Ms Liyani arrest and bail
sections.summary: Ms Liyani was arrested on 2 December 2016 and spent almost four years in a HOME shelter, with HOME posting $15,000 bail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ms Liyani was arrested on 2 December 2016 and spent almost four years in a shelter managed by the NGO, HOME.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While waiting for her case to be concluded, she was fortunate that HOME was able to find someone to post bail of $15,000 for her.

sections.label: Liyani sentence and wait
sections.summary: Ms Liyani was sentenced by the State Court to 26 months in prison, less than the four years she waited for the case's outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ms Liyani was sentenced by the State Court to 26 months in prison, which was less than the four years she spent waiting for the outcome of the case.

sections.label: Minister on Liyani's fees
sections.summary: The Minister for Law said Ms Liyani's fees would have come up to $150,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister for Law has mentioned that Ms Liyani's fees would have come up to $150,000.

sections.label: Working group outcome question
sections.summary: The passage asks what the outcome of this working group is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is the outcome of this working group?

sections.label: Why judicial system efficaciousness matters
sections.summary: The speaker asks why the overall efficaciousness of the judicial system should matter, citing eroded rule of law worldwide and in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I actually wish to take a step back and ask the question of not so much where some areas within the system appear to fall short, but why we should care about the overall efficaciousness of the judicial system, which goes far beyond the events surrounding Parti Liyani's case.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
